They were given combat tasks, but very often these groups, inverted commas, protected the so-called smuggler's convoys, because smuggling was flourishing between Zepa and Gorazde, particularly cigarettes, alcohol, and other items and food stuffs that were lacking in Zepa. And Gorazde was to a large extent receiving its deliveries from Sarajevo, so for those reasons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. President, I didn't mean to interrupt the answer. I thought the witness had completed his answer. I just wanted to -- perhaps it will help my learned friend save a little bit of her time again as we've stated from day one of this trial, the Prosecution does not dispute that there were excursions and incursions from the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves by armed groups of Muslim fighters throughout this period of time. That is not in dispute in case and never has been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So please avoid -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree with what Mr. Thayer has said. I have no intention to demonstrate that these groups were there, but I would like to talk about the actions and the attitude of the Republika Srpska because the Prosecution when it presented its case mentioned a number of things about Gorazde, which are not contained in the indictment. This is why I felt it was important, but whatever the case may be, I shall not spend a lot of time on this. And the other thing is I would like to say is that this document, which relates to my cross-examination, are the documents which are the witness's documents which he signed personally as a commander of the Visegrad tactical group; and I believe it's very important to hear -- for the Trial Chamber to hear questions put on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: General, you heard I would like to show you three to four documents, and we shall address the details a little later. I would now like to show you 5D1265.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Before seeing this document, I would need to see document 5D1029.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The document that will come up on your screen very shortly, is a document stemming from the staff of the Main Staff of the 14th of November 1993. If you look at the part of this document which starts with, "On the 11th of November," in B/C/S it discusses the communications between Visegrad and Rogatica. It's right in the middle of the page. What I'm interested in is this, is this the situation which you mentioned awhile ago when you were talking about your order which was dated the 12th of November?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could now see Exhibit number 5D1265. Once again, could we see the second page in English and the bottom of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you see your name on this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show the witness paragraph -- in other words, the preamble to this order. This is on page 1 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is another situation which is very similar to the one you described to us a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last order which is Exhibit 5D1266.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This again is an order coming from the Visegrad tactical group dated the 14th of December 1995 [sic]. What I'm interested in is this, the preamble, and the passage which reads: [In English] "The Muslim forces are preparing an attack on our positions from the directions of Zepa and Gorazde, with the aim of relieving their forces in the Olovo and Teocak sectors."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to correct the record, it's 1993. It's a mistake in the English translation as well, the original is obviously 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, I think that's correct. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite, right, I believe it was my mistake. I think I said 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is not so much the fact that the Muslim forces were coming out of Gorazde and Zepa. But this objective i.e., to help their forces in Olovo be and Teocak. Could you tell us where Olovo and Teocak is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Olovo is to the southwest of my area of responsibility, that is from Han Pijesak, Vlasenica, in the direction of Tuzla and Sarajevo. So Sarajevo, Olovo, Kladanj, Tuzla, that's the direction. Teocak, is an area to the southwest of Bijeljina and Zvornik. That's the area of Teocak. Evidently, at that time there was intensive fighting going on in these two areas, and it was precisely for this reason that armed units in Srebrenica and Zepa were given the tasks of carrying out sabotage activities in the area around the protected areas in order to relieve the armed units in these two sectors.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Save for this objective, did you know in 1993 whether the Muslim forces in the enclaves, I mean all the enclaves, Zepa, Srebrenica and Gorazde, do you know whether they had a specific objective?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: After the protected areas were established, those of Srebrenica, Zepa and Gorazde; and after UNPROFOR forces entered Srebrenica and Zepa, whereas the Gorazde enclave was not put into that function, the forces there prepared to take that area of Podrinje, Rudo, Visegrad, and so on, and to completely join up Gorazde and Zepa. This way, they would gain a compact territory from central Bosnia and via Sarajevo, Gorazde, Visegrad and Zepa, and that would create the conditions in joint action with forces from Tuzla -- from the direction of Tuzla to take all of Podrinje. We received intelligence showing that such an operation was being prepared in May in the direction of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit number 5D1169.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is an order stemming from the Main Staff of the army dated the 22nd of May 1993. You have just talked about information received by the intelligence services. Do you think this order has anything to do with that information?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, can the witness be shown item 3, please. This is right at the bottom in English. This would be on page 2, the second part of paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I reply? Before this order arrived, I carried out a detailed analysis of the situation in the area of responsibility of my tactical group, and after the protected areas were established. After this detailed analysis, I submitted this information to the superior command along with certain proposals as to what should be done in order to put the situation completely under control, and to stabilize the situation especially with respect to Gorazde. One of the bases for the taking of specific measures was my report on the concrete situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to clarify one point. Could the witness be shown the date of this order, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Here we are talking about the 22nd of May 1993. I don't think it is disputed that Zepa and -- Srebrenica and Zepa were already safe areas. Could you tell us what the situation was like in Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: I have already said that. The Muslim forces in Gorazde took advantage of the signing of the agreement on protected areas in order to prepare for offensive combat activities. It is my personal opinion that it was not in their interest for Gorazde to be given full protected area status where UNPROFOR forces would come in. It was sufficient for them to have five or six UN observers who would monitor the situation and report on any activity by Serb forces around Gorazde, whereas their own activities, they either could not or did not want to monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just to be quite sure. At the time, was UNPROFOR and the forces of UNPROFOR, were they in Gorazde at the time this order was issued?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Only monitors.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown page 2 in B/C/S. This will be on page 3 in the English at the bottom of the page. In B/C/S and in English this is at the bottom of the page. Can you see the bottom of the page, could the witness be shown the bottom of the page, please. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The paragraph which begins with, "In the second stage." In this paragraph, we see that what has been requested are the conditions, the prerequisite conditions to be able to disarm the Muslim forces and make sure the civilian population can leave for central Bosnia or stay in town if it recognizes the Serb authority. What was the overall policy of the army of the Republika Srpska when it entered a town in which the Muslims lived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: What I am aware of, and I do know this, is that in all orders and especially in preparing combat activities, emphasis was always laid on taking into account possible casualties among the civilian population, and to reduce such casualties to a minimum, especially in built-up areas, or to avoid them, if at all possible. It's evident from this order that in every territory which was being liberated, the Muslim population was given the option of staying. But if they decided to leave and move to territories under the control of their army, they could do so. In my own experience, I never found any civilians in any of the territories we liberated. Evidently, even before intensive fighting began, the civilian population was moved out of the area where the fighting would take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau Ivanovic. Could you could help me finding the passage in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there is a mistake in English: "In the first stage" and then the part I was interested in where the last three sentences, "... creating conditions to disarm the Muslim formations and enable the civilian population to move out of central Bosnia..." This is on page 3, the last three lines, but I believe that must be a mistake in the translation. I don't mean these three lines but prior to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I asked this question because I couldn't find, "In the second stage" at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I realised that when I was asking the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You stated, General, that you never encountered a situation where the Army of Republika Srpska would have found any Muslim population on the territory where they arrived, but are you aware of cases where the Muslim population remained on a territory now in control of the Army of Republika Srpska? Not now but during the war, a territory that during the war was under the control of the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: In my area from the very beginning of the war until nearly the end of the war there were four villages which were purely Muslim, according to their ethnicity, this was between Visegrad and Rogatica. They belonged to Rogatica municipality and these villages were Satorovici, Osovo, Okruglo, and Burati. That population remained living on territory controlled by the army of Republika Srpska and under the Serbian civilian authorities. A large influence was exerted on them to remain by a retired general of the former JNA, Asim Hodzic, who was advanced in years; but when combat began in Bosnia-Herzegovina, he was living in the village of Satorovici. As he was in poor health, I had occasion to meet him personally when he was being transported from Rogatica via Visegrad and Uzice to Belgrade at the military medical [Realtime transcript read in error, "military academy."] academy. The population in these villages remained peaceful, and they lived there until the second half of 1994 peacefully. Then they moved away probably in the direction of Sarajevo or somewhere in central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President if we could have spellings for those villages for the record since they came out kind of fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay thank you. Who is going do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was about to come back to that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, would you please repeat very slowly the names of these villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes. These were the villages of Satorovici, S-A-T-O-R-O-V-I-C-I; Okruglo, O-K-R-U-G-L-O; Osovo, O-S-O-V-O; and Burati, B-U-R-A-T-I.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just one more clarification, please, Asim Hodzic this retired general, what was his nationality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Asim Hodzic, he was a Muslim by nationality.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I believe that we need to correct the transcript here again. Page 52 line 5, you mention the fact that he was translated to Belgrade from Rogatica via Visegrad and Uzice. Could you tell us where he went to Belgrade, to what institution he was taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: He went to the military medical academy to undergo medical treatment there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You mentioned this civilian population that remained for the major part of the war in territories controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska. Did this population have any problem where it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Occasionally they suffer the provocations from individuals or small groups who disturbed those people and exerted verbal pressure on them to get them to move away from the territory and from their villages. I know that the commander of the first Rogatica Brigade intervened with the civilian authorities more than once to have the civilian police patrol those villages more often and protect those people from possible individual provocations.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 5D1030.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I believe that the document speaks for itself, but I'd like to clarify one thing. Did you know Major Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In March 1994, when this document was drafted, who was his immediate superior, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you once again tell us who his immediate superior was because the answer we got in English was, "Yes," but I believe that you intended to say something else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: His immediate superior was Colonel Dragisa Masal.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just before the break, I'd like to deal with civilian population again. Throughout your career in the army of Republika Srpska were you ever faced with situations in which the ABiH used its own population for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes. I did acquire such information, especially when I was commanding the Visegrad tactical group in the Gorazde area. The civilian population was used in large numbers in the rear and to help the frontline, primarily to carry ammunition to the combat line to fortify defence positions, dig trenches, shelters and so on. We learned this from several Serb civilians who remained in Gorazde until 1994. Not only were these Serbs who remained in Gorazde used for these purposes, but the Muslim population was also used for that in large numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: With respect to these Serb civilians remained in Gorazde until 1994, do you know whether they remained in Gorazde of their own free will, or whether they were forced to remain there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were two villages in Gorazde which were Serb villages in the western part of the area around Gorazde in the part of Sarajevo towards Grebak, Igman, and Sarajevo. I think that one of these villages was called Bukovica or something like that. And based on the facts we obtained from the Serbs who had fled from Gorazde and from the survivors who left in 19.94 they were completely cut off and were unable to leave their villages. They were very far from other Serb territories and Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau, any time you wish to stop, just let us know, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could the witness be shown Exhibit 5D1000.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Before the break we were talking about the use of the civilian population for military purposes. Here we have a document dating back to the period prior to you joining the Visegrad tactical group. Could you have a quick look at this document and tell us whether what was described in this document corresponds to what you yourself saw or were aware of.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes, completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: General, in this trial we've reviewed a number of directives. I'd like to show you Directive number 5. That's Exhibit 5D1201. This is dated 25th of June 1993. First of all, at the time were you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to see this directive, but I did receive an order from my superior command relating to this directive.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to page 4 in B/C/S, and page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is the task assigned to the Drina Corps: [In English] "Hold remaining [indiscernible] and Gorazde, Zepa and Srebrenica completely under siege and [indiscernible]." [Interpretation] I believe there is an error in the English translation because in the original version in B/C/S mention is made of a constant siege. Could you please explain why it was necessary to keep Muslim forces under constant siege?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Based on what is contained in this directive and knowing, or, rather, remembering the task that I had been assigned was that owing to their ongoing activities and particularly offensive attacks coming from the direction of Gorazde, all the units were requested, or, rather, ordered to keep these forces under constant blockade with a view to preventing their incursions into the rear part of our territory, and with a view to establishing control between the protected areas or enclaves. In early 1993, or, rather, in April and May 1993, all the three enclaves were fully physical separated. However, the activities taking place there, and particularly the activities of large or small terrorist and sabotage groups, and some extensive offensive actions as well, they attempted to keep the communication between the enclaves under their permanent control, which is to enable their movement and coordinated actions between the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to another topic now. You've already mentioned UNPROFOR and convoys. Do you remember whether UNPROFOR convoys and convoys from humanitarian associations were controlled, were checked in 1993 when you were the commander of the Visegrad tactical group.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Convoys headed towards Zepa and Gorazde passed through my zone. The order of my superior command based on the order of the Main Staff, which I very often received directly, it was very precisely stipulated in what way and at which point the movement and the cargo of the convoys would be checked. And I'm referring to convoys entering the protected zones. This order set down precisely who is to carry out the inspection, what kind of teams are going to inspect them, and their composition, how the teams should be trained to do that, what kind of inspection they are going to apply to each convoy depending on whether it was an UNHCR convoy or some other humanitarian organisations convoy. And finally, least but not least, how UNPROFOR convoys were to be inspected. All the commands were informed about the contents of this order and detailed preparations were made of teams who were to be directly involved in the inspection of these convoys.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to show you Exhibit 5D768.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is an order related to the movement of UNPROFOR and UNHCR convoys related to humanitarian aid convoys in Republika Srpska. This is an order from the Main Staff dated 2nd of April 1993. We can see that this order was sent directly to the Visegrad tactical group.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to page 2 of this order. Page 2 in English as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Earlier on you talked about various types of inspections for UNPROFOR convoys and humanitarian aid organisations convoys. At items 5(a) and 5(b), do we have the definition or the description of how inspections should be conducted depending on which convoys we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Items 5(a) and 5(b) clearly described, and in detail, how inspections of both are going to be carried out logistically of humanitarian aid convoys and logistically for UNPROFOR convoys. What was in practice undertaken by my command was that pursuant to this order, we prepared some pocket-size manuals for each member of the team participating in the inspection of the convoys, just to remind them on the spot not to deviate from this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn to page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: General, please look at item 9. This is related to the prohibition of the transport of certain types of materials, equipment, radio and video equipment. Could you explain why video equipment was prohibited?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Radio devices and video equipment were prohibited from bringing in with the exception of the radio devices attached to UNPROFOR vehicles. This kind of equipment was under ban and prohibited from bringing them into the protected area because those were technical means that were probably intended for the enemy side and their troops. As for electronic and radio devices, that was the case. However, video cameras were most strictly forbidden because no serious command will allow its units, troop, positions, defence positions and infrastructure, weapons or any other details to be filmed in the area where they are carrying out their combat operations. The reason being that all these footage could have been abused during combat and also after combat operations have ceased.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Before item 6, at the very top of the page in English we see that it was necessary to record the quantities of fuel, and if we go back to the previous page, we'll see that we are dealing here with humanitarian aid convoys. Was there a specific reason for this to record the quantities of fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes, there was a reason for that. The humanitarian aid convoys very often carried a larger quantity of fuel than was actually needed for their vehicles. This fuel was then sold both to the army and civilians, but primarily to the Muslim army in Zepa and Gorazde, and probably in Srebrenica as well, but I'm now talking about Zepa and Gorazde because I know these details relating to these two towns.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We saw that this order was dated 2nd of April before the establishment of protected areas, but after that, once the protected areas had been established did you receive further orders related to the passage of convoys?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D804, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We have an order dated 10 December 1993. I'd like you to turn to item 3.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the checkpoints that you had in your area of responsibility, did you comply with that order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: As much as was possible, and it is true that these inspection teams who also monitored the movement of UNPROFOR were made up of the best officers of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Please have a look at item 4 now. That's on the next page in the English version of the document. I'm interested in what we see at the very end where it says that the content of checks are defined by two orders from August 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When a convoy arrived at a checkpoint, would the officers who were there at the checkpoint, would they know exactly how they were about to proceed with this convoy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: All members of the inspection teams were thoroughly trained beforehand to carry out the task in general, and for each convoy they would receive specific orders as well from the Main Staff and the superior command, the command of the Drina Corps. We regularly received a 24-hour advance notice of the arrival of the convoys specifying the exact time of their entering the area of responsibility of a specific command or unit, and what is the composition of that convoy. In that way, we were able to prepare ourselves way ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had like to show you Exhibit 5D805.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is information coming from the Main Staff related to the passage of convoys. This document bears the same date as the previous one.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: This is precisely a notice that each unit through whose zone the convoy was supposed to pass would receive.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 3 in English, and page 2, the bottom of page 2 in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If you look at this very last sentence, "Carry out a detailed check..." and so on and so forth. Would the orders mentioned earlier, the orders dating back to August 1993, would these orders apply to this convoy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Yes, both are to this specific convoy and to any other convoy about which there was suspicion of its carrying something that was not contained in the declaration or the announcement of the movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If you now turn to the paragraph that is just before this last sentence. The paragraph that comes just before this last sentence, the bottom of page 2 in English. I believe that you've already mentioned this, but have you encountered similar situations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL
utterances.text: Several times during checks of humanitarian aid convoys, we encountered a situation that in the original package of the declared goods, some other items were packed. There were instances in which cameras and still cameras were hidden, and once or twice the original packaging containing food we also found some ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm very sorry, could we stop now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Mr. Masal, we have to stop today here and we will continue on Monday. Before you leave this courtroom, however, I need to advise you that one of our rules that you need to observe in the strictest manner is that between now and when you resume your testimony on Monday, you do not communicate with anyone on the subject matter of your testimony. When I say you must not communicate with anyone, it means either you or if anyone tries to contact you and communicate with you on this subject matter. Have I made myself understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we stand adjourned until Monday, 9.00 in the morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st of December 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
